dedupe_keys.name: fengjiaping landslide electrical soil and uav topography observations

description: The Zenodo release collects measurements from the Fengjiaping landslide in Gansu Province, China. The article describes self-potential sensing at 86 electrodes, four electrical-resistivity tomography lines, soil temperature and moisture measurements, and UAV-derived surface topography. The public repository lists thirteen small files or archives, including gridded soil and elevation products and raw SP and ERT packages, under CC BY 4.0. These observations can test groundwater-flow and slope-instability assumptions in corridor-risk simulations, but they are one landslide site, not a regional inventory of road closures or failure frequency. Electrode placement, survey dates, inversion choices and a single depth for some soil sensors are limitations for transferring results to other slopes. A reviewer-assessed use is checking subsurface water-pathway states before modelling rainfall-triggered slope effects near infrastructure. data-cedd-hk-slopes-landslide-incidents is a related slope event source from another region, without direct linkage. No raw archive or raster was downloaded.
